questions.stem: What element is present in all organic compounds?
questions.explanation: All organic compounds contain carbon. Carbon atoms can form four covalent bonds, allowing them to create a huge variety of molecules including chains, branches, and rings.

options.text: A list of all known organic compounds
A group of elements in the same period
A family of organic compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties
A series of reactions that produce the same product

questions.explanation: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds that share the same general formula, have similar chemical properties, and differ from one member to the next by a CH₂ group.

questions.stem: What is a functional group in organic chemistry?

options.text: The total number of carbon atoms in a molecule
An atom or group of atoms that determines the chemical properties of a compound
The state of the compound at room temperature

questions.explanation: A functional group is a specific atom or group of atoms within a molecule that determines the chemical reactions and properties of that compound (e.g., -OH in alcohols, C=C in alkenes).

questions.stem: Why can carbon form so many different compounds?

options.text: Carbon can form four covalent bonds and bond to itself to make chains, branches, and rings
Carbon can only bond with hydrogen
Carbon is the most abundant element

questions.explanation: Carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell and can form 4 covalent bonds. It can bond to other carbon atoms to form long chains, branched structures, and rings, creating millions of different compounds.

questions.stem: What type of formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a molecule?
questions.explanation: The empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound. For example, the empirical formula of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is CH₂O.

questions.stem: What does a displayed formula show?

options.text: All the bonds between all the atoms in the molecule
Only the types of atoms present

questions.explanation: A displayed formula shows all the atoms and all the bonds between them in a molecule, giving a clear picture of how the atoms are connected.

questions.stem: As the chain length of molecules in a homologous series increases, what generally happens to the boiling point?
questions.explanation: As chain length increases, molecules have more electrons and greater surface area, leading to stronger intermolecular forces. More energy is needed to overcome these forces, so boiling points increase.
